source_snapshot.items: BMC Shell (SSH) - Verify access control settings
source_snapshot.procedure: Enable BMC Shell via SSH in WebUI and prove a login succeeds; disable it, wait, and prove login is not allowed.
source_snapshot.criteria: SSH console login is allowed when enabled and denied when disabled.
source_snapshot.script: No Master command; 10 attended/5 machine minutes; unique row/code/variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; drives WebUI and SSH attempts, recognizes lockout risk and restoration but lacks causal denial proof.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CRITICAL; adds dedicated account, bounded fresh sessions, independent recovery, error classification and restore.

old_problem: The source does not bind a safe test account, apply timing, policy-specific rejection oracle, existing-session behavior or recovery. A generic failed login may be network or credential failure, and disabling the only management path could lock out the operator.
disposition_reason: The enabled-allow/disabled-deny matrix is explicit. ED-03/15/20/24 permit account, propagation delay, expected SSH error class and original/final state as project bindings. Dedicated identity, one fresh attempt per state, UI/API applied-state readback and independent management recovery make the procedure review-complete without guessing OEM policy semantics.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2225, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2226 / Wistron-BMC Sanity-00009-V002 / 5c381b355e391034 was directly read from XLSX and its historical record.
Use a dedicated non-sole-admin test account and prove an independent WebUI/serial/physical recovery administrator before disabling SSH.
Record original policy and active sessions; enable, wait for authoritative applied-state readback, open one fresh trusted SSH session and execute only a harmless identity command.
Close the enabled-state session; disable, confirm applied state and perform exactly one new connection attempt, classifying DNS/route/TCP/host-key/authentication/policy outcomes.
Observe any deliberately retained preexisting session separately because new-connection denial and existing-session termination are different behaviors.
Restore the original policy and prove recovery access; preserve security/audit evidence without clearing it.
Stop on wrong target, unexpected access loss, unclassified denial or restore failure; no credential brute force or automatic retry.
No WebUI change, SSH attempt, policy mutation, restore, retry, recovery or DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: BMC SSH policy enabled/disabled enforcement and restoration
test_case.purpose: Verify with a dedicated account that fresh BMC SSH access succeeds only when the BMC Shell policy is enabled, is rejected for the approved policy-specific reason when disabled, and the original policy is safely restored.
required_package: Exact BMC/firmware, policy location/readback and management interface
Dedicated test account/role, trusted host key and harmless identity command
Applied-state propagation timing, enabled/disabled error oracle and existing-session contract
Independent recovery administrator/path, original/final policy and maximum one attempt per state
test_case.test_command: After independent recovery is proven and the state change is authorized, record the original policy; enable BMC Shell, wait for applied-state readback and perform one fresh trusted SSH login with the dedicated account; close it, disable the policy, confirm applied state and perform one bounded fresh connection attempt while classifying the failure; record existing-session behavior separately, then restore and verify the original policy and recovery access.
test_case.expected_result: Enabled policy permits the dedicated account's fresh authenticated session and harmless command; disabled policy rejects a fresh session with the approved causal signature; existing-session behavior matches the signed contract; original policy and management access are restored.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires both fresh-session states, applied-policy proof, causal denial classification and verified restoration. Wrong endpoint, unrelated network/credential failure, unexpected existing-session behavior, broader lockout or restore failure is FAIL. Missing account/oracle/recovery blocks execution, not review.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until an independent recovery path and non-sole-admin test account are proven.
Use trusted host identity and secret-safe authentication; one fresh attempt per state only.
Do not modify other policies, test other users, clear logs or retry credentials.
Stop on wider access loss, ambiguous denial or restore failure.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, BMC firmware, endpoint and account role
Enabled SSH negotiation/authentication/identity-command success and clean close
Disabled attempt's transport/SSH/auth/policy evidence plus existing-session observation
Security/audit logs, independent recovery proof and final state
test_case.recovery: If SSH or management access behaves unexpectedly, do not retry. Preserve audit/transport evidence and use the pre-proven independent WebUI/serial/physical administrator to restore the original policy and verify BMC health.

source_conflict.reason: The source coherently specifies an enabled/disabled SSH access matrix; missing account and error semantics are runtime bindings.

blocked.reason: Policy purpose and two states are clear; safe identity, causal oracle and recovery can be supplied.

pending.execution_status: REVIEW RESOLVED AS PARAMETERIZED TWO-STATE ACCESS-CONTROL TEST; POLICY CHANGE AUTHORIZATION AND RECOVERY REQUIRED; NO POLICY CHANGE, SSH ATTEMPT, RESTORE, RETRY, RECOVERY OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED
pending.owner: BMC security owner and authorized management/recovery operator
pending.unlock_condition: Sign the account, policy/error semantics, one-attempt matrix, original/final state and independent recovery; absence blocks execution but not review resolution.
